Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told reporters that planning is underway to hold a regional meeting with the participation of the littoral states of the Persian Gulf. Referring to Iran’s longstanding efforts to build trust and cooperation among the countries of the region in order to strengthen peace and stability in the region, free from the harmful and divisive interference of actors from outside the region, the Foreign Ministry Spokesperson described the initiative to hold a meeting of foreign ministers of the littoral states of the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman as an important development in this regard. He expressed hope that the event would pave the way for greater understanding among the countries of the region and help strengthen shared regional security. According to Baghaei, the meeting will be held in Oman on Monday with the participation of Iran, Iraq and other littoral states of the Persian Gulf. In addition to other regional issues, the meeting will also discuss and exchange views on the outcome of the Iran-Oman negotiations regarding the designation of safe routes for commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The Foreign Ministry Spokesperson also recalled the understanding reached between Iran and Oman regarding temporary shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz, stressing that the Islamic Republic of Iran considers itself committed to efforts to ensure the security of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. However, he said that, naturally, as long as the aggressive actions and unlawful interference by the United States, including the naval blockade and economic warfare, continue, the security of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz cannot be guaranteed.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Pakistan Army Chief hold phone conversation
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Field Marshal Asim Munir, Commander of the Pakistani Army, held a phone conversation on Thursday evening. During the call, the two sides reviewed the latest regional developments and exchanged views on the escalation of tensions and increasing insecurity in the region and their consequences for regional peace and stability. The two sides also, stressing the need for vigilance and coordination among regional countries regarding ongoing developments, emphasized the use of shared capacities to help establish lasting peace and security in the region.

item.title: Iranian Parliaments Economic Commission holds meeting with Foreign Minister
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi attended a meeting of the Economic Commission of Iran's Parliament as part of his continued participation in meetings of the Parliament's specialized commissions, where he held discussions and exchanged views with members of the commission on the most important developments and issues related to the country's foreign policy and economy. At the meeting, a report was presented on the latest regional developments, particularly the course of talks and negotiations with the Omani side. Hamid Ghanbari, Deputy Foreign Minister for Economic Diplomacy, also presented a report on the latest status and aspects of the recent US sanctions and their effects and consequences on the country's economic and trade sectors. The Foreign Minister subsequently responded to questions and some ambiguities raised by the lawmakers.

item.title: Foreign Ministry statement on developments related to Yemen
item.description: The Islamic Republic of Iran reaffirms its principled and steadfast position on the need to respect the independence, national sovereignty and territorial integrity of Yemen, and to end the illegal and inhumane blockade of the country. Undoubtedly, security and stability in West Asia and the Red Sea region cannot be achieved without respecting the legitimate rights and dignity of the great people of Yemen. What is currently happening in Yemen cannot be separated from the developments of the past more than decade. The great and noble people of Yemen, as heirs to a brilliant and historic civilization who have always played a decisive and honorable role in the history of the region and the world, have the right to live a dignified life, free from pressure, intimidation and an unjust blockade, and their national sovereignty and territorial integrity must be fully respected. item.title: Iran FM holds phone call with new OIC Secretary-General
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi held a phone conversation on Monday with Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, the newly appointed Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The Foreign Minister congratulated Ould Cheikh Ahmed on his election as OIC Secretary-General and wished him success in his new position. Araghchi expressed hope that, by drawing on the organization’s capacities, the new Secretary-General would play a role in strengthening the unity and coordination of Islamic countries in addressing developments and challenges facing the Muslim world. During the call, Araghchi briefed the OIC Secretary-General on the latest regional developments following the US and Israeli regime’s aggression against Iran, stressing the need for responsible action by Islamic countries in response to violations of Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the need to counter the use of force and aggression. The Foreign Minister also referred to the critical circumstances and challenges facing the Muslim world, particularly the continuation of the Israeli regime’s aggression and crimes in Palestine and Lebanon. He stressed the need for firm support for the rights of the Palestinian and Lebanese peoples and for Islamic countries to adopt united and effective positions on these developments. Araghchi also invited the new OIC Secretary-General to visit Tehran and expressed hope that the visit would take place at the earliest appropriate opportunity.
